source_refs.note: Book p. 50: 4.2.3 Scalar Multiplication (kA = [ka_ij]) with the pink Note box A + A + ... to n terms = nA. Worked illustration, Teaching notes, Key points and Common mistake are ours.

blocks.text: Ab ek aur aasan magar bohat kaam ka operation: scalar multiplication, yani kisi aam number se poori matrix ko zarb dena. Aage determinants, inverse aur matrix equations mein yeh har jagah aayega.

Kitab ki definition: agar \(A = [a_{ij}]\) ek \(m \times n\) matrix ho aur \(k\) koi real ya complex number ho, to \(k\) aur \(A\) ka product, jise \(kA\) likhte hain, woh matrix hai jo \(A\) ki har entry ko \(k\) se zarb dene se banti hai, yani

blocks.text_alt: k A equals the matrix of k times a i j

blocks.text: Zaahir hai ke \(kA\) ka order bhi \(m \times n\) hi hai, kyun ke na koi row barhi na koi column; sirf har khane ka number \(k\) guna ho gaya.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Agar \(n\) koi positive integer ho, to \(A + A + A + \ldots\) \(n\) terms tak \(= nA\).

Is note ki wajah samjhiye: \(A + A + A\) mein har khane ki entry teen baar jama hoti hai, aur kisi number ko teen baar jama karna use 3 se zarb dene ke barabar hai, jaise \(5 + 5 + 5 = 3 \times 5\). Yani matrices mein bhi baar baar jama karna zarb hi hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Akele number ko scalar kehte hain, taa ke use matrix se alag pehchana ja sake. Scalar se zarb mein kabhi order check nahin karna parta: har entry ek hi number se zarb hoti hai aur shakal wahi rehti hai. Socho ek dukaan ki price list jis mein har cheez ki qeemat double ho gayi: poori list (matrix) 2 se zarb ho gayi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin. \(K = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\) ho to \(3K\) kya hai?
\[3K = \begin{bmatrix} 3(1) & 3(-2) \\ 3(0) & 3(4) \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}3 & -6 \\ 0 & 12\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: har entry 3 se zarb hui; \(3 \times (-2) = -6\) aur \(3 \times 0 = 0\).
Tasdeeq (Note ki madad se): \(K + K + K\) mein row 1, column 2 par \(-2 - 2 - 2 = -6\) aata hai, aur row 2, column 2 par \(4 + 4 + 4 = 12\). Bilkul \(3K\) jaisa.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Teen khaas scalars yaad rakhiye: \(1A = A\) (kuch nahin badalta); \((-1)A = -A\), yani har entry ka sign ulta, jo subtraction (4.2.2) mein kaam aaya; aur \(0A = O\), usi order ki null matrix.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(-2\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\) kya hai?
Jawab: \(\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 6 \\ 0 & -10 \end{bmatrix}\). Negative scalar se har sign badal jata hai: \(-2 \times -3 = 6\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(kA = [ka_{ij}]\): har entry ko \(k\) se zarb dein.
2. \(kA\) ka order wahi jo \(A\) ka; order ki koi shart nahin.
3. \(A + A + \ldots\) (\(n\) terms) \(= nA\); \((-1)A = -A\); \(0A = O\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Sirf pehli row ya ek hi entry ko \(k\) se zarb dena. Aage determinants mein ek row wala qaida aayega, lekin matrix ke liye har entry zarb hoti hai. Dono ko mila dena aam ghalti hai.
2. Signs: \(3 \times (-2) = -6\), aur \((-2) \times (-3) = 6\).
3. \(kA\) (matrix) ko \(k + A\) samajh lena; number aur matrix ka jama define hi nahin.
